On Sun, 22 Dec 2024 at 00:11, 'Ling' via lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
Dear ALL, 

I have 3 questions!!! Need your help!!THANKS A LOT!!!

My model is f=~f1
j=~j1+j2+j3
k=~k1+k2
z=~j+k
(z is second level factor variable and f only have 1 measure)
I need to run SEM for this model. 


1. I need to set f=~square root( f1's Cronbach's Alpha) and f~~variance of f1(1-Cronbach's Alpha)*f
But I am struggling with how to get Cronbach's Alpha for f1. Could anyone help? I would appreciate if you could provide any instructions or codes.
You don't want Cronbach's alpha, you want the reliability. You can't estimate the reliability with one measure on one occasion.
2. Should I get Cronbach's Alpha and variance from a CFA model or should I estimate the variance for each j1 j2 j3 individually like var(j1)?
I'm not sure what you mean here. I don't know why you want to estimate the reliability of j.
3. How to deal with 2 order factor? How to estimate the Cronbach's Alpha and variance for second order factor? Do I just do the same as first order like what I do with j1 j2 j3 var(j1)?

Your second order factor seems to have only two indicators? It's therefore not identified unless you constrain the loadings to be equal, and that is then equivalent to a model with a correlation between the latent variables. What are you trying to do with the second order factor?

Jeremy
